notes.summary: New unverified partial theorem: all finite weighted rank-one balanced tree graphs times any complete affine factor have finite rational-domain real-PAPC envelopes and full recursive contact for every positive-growth real-PA PC reference and every bounded real-PA obstacle, including nonseparable functions. Cyclic graph cylinders and original P05.2 classification remain open; no literal-category inference.
notes.detailedSummary: The proof reconstructs all used dependencies. Full actual saturated vertex lattices are amalgamated along primitive bounded-edge lattices on a tree, preserving every actual rational-endpoint PCC with real coefficients and all local recursive divisor indices. Weighted recursive scalar affine supports and partial Legendre infima supply finite ambient convex majorants for every raw PC competitor without assuming its continuity. A global obstacle epigraph hull, with rational spatial generators and real heights, identifies the actual envelope and yields a finite rational spatial complex. Ambient supports establish PAPC against every nonnegative local real cycle in every positive dimension; P+1/j gives uniform decreasing regularization. At every noncontact atom, independent branch complements force grouped generator sums into outgoing edge lines. Their positive branch functionals and unique local relation give a flat subspace spanning the local graph span, hence quotient dimension at most m<d=m+1; otherwise a nonzero affine-factor flat gives common lineality. Both force the entire recursive top divisor to vanish, including vertex fibres and lower-face terms. The complete integral is zero. The theorem permits arbitrary finite tree size, rational weights and lengths, local valences and nonsaturated ray-generated junction lattices. A triangular cyclic example proves only failure of the naive lift via a nonzero formal period, not an envelope/contact counterexample. Three exact finite diagnostics and two successful PDF passes are retained; they do not verify the mathematics. Status is partial and original P05.2 remains open.

---
title: "Envelope contact on arbitrary finite weighted tree cylinders"
author: "Unverified P05.2 partial research result"
date: "3 October 2026"
---

## Exact result and remaining scope

The original P05.2 classification remains open. This draft proves the following special case, extending the specified two-vertex example to arbitrary finite trees, rational weights, higher valences and nonsaturated ray-generated local lattices. It does not assume an earlier theorem or review.

**Theorem.** Let $G$ be a finite pure balanced rational polyhedral graph in a lattice vector space $N_{G,\mathbb R}$. Edge weights $w_e$ are positive rational numbers, and outgoing directions $v_{v,e}$ are the actual saturated primitive directions. Assume that every connected component is a tree after the unbounded ends are regarded as leaves, and that at every vertex
$$
\{a\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^{E(v)}:\sum_ea_ev_{v,e}=0\}
=\mathbb R_{\geq0}(w_e)_e. \tag{1}
$$
Let $E$ be a complete rational affine space of dimension $m$ with its actual lattice, put $X=G\times E$, use the direct product lattice and inherited edge weights, and put $d=m+1$.

Here $\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbb R}$ means continuous real-affine pieces on a **finite rational spatial complex**, rather than arbitrary real polyhedral domains. For every $\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbb R}(X)\cap\mathrm{PC}(X)$ positive at infinity and every bounded $u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbb R}(X)$, the raw envelope $P=P_\gamma(u)$ is itself $\mathrm{PAPC}_{\mathbb R}(X,\gamma)$ on a finite rational spatial complex. In particular it is uniformly decreasing real-regularizable, and its full recursive measure satisfies
$$
\operatorname{supp}(P^d\cdot[X])\subset\{P=\gamma+u\},\qquad
\int_X(P-\gamma-u)\,\mathrm{MA}_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbb R}(P)=0,
\quad \mathrm{MA}_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbb R}(P)=P^d\cdot[X]. \tag{2}
$$
Both reference and obstacle may be genuinely nonseparable. There is no bound on the number or rational lengths of the bounded edges or on $m$. No unimodularity of a collection of outgoing rays is imposed. Cycles are excluded; they remain an unresolved part of the graph-cylinder assignment. No literal integral-slope conclusion or analytic realization is claimed. The theorem is an unverified mathematical draft, not a formal or independently certified result.

## Definitions and checked source boundaries

BMPS denotes Botero--Mazzon--Pille-Schneider, *Monge--Ampère measures on balanced polyhedral spaces*, arXiv:2603.08664v1, manuscript dated 10 March 2026. We inspected its definitions and the proof bodies specified here. We reconstruct the algebra and convex facts used below instead of importing its larger dependency chain.

Definitions 3.2--3.3 mean the following actual PCCs. The endpoints $x_i$ are in $X\cap N_{\mathbb Q}$; the coefficients $a_i\geq0$ are real with $\sum a_i=1$; the centre is the actual point $x=\sum a_ix_i$; and on some rational structure there are cells $\tau\preceq\sigma_i$ with $x\in\tau$ and $x_i\in\sigma_i$. A finite raw PC function $h:X\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $h(x)\leq\sum a_ih(x_i)$ for every such combination, on every permitted structure. Raw competitors are not assumed continuous.

Definition 6.2 gives
$$
P_\gamma(u)(x)=\sup\{h(x):h\in\mathrm{PC}(X),\ h\leq\gamma+u,
\ h\leq\gamma+C_h\text{ for some }C_h\in\mathbb R\}. \tag{3}
$$
Definition 4.15's positivity at infinity means strictly positive reference slope on every nonzero recession vector of every reference affine cell. Definition 3.14's growth class is $\gamma+O(1)$, with a two-sided bounded difference. Definition 3.1 tests PAPC against **every** nonnegative local balanced cycle of every positive dimension on ordinary open subsets. We use real coefficients and real cycle weights explicitly. Definition 2.28's literal class has integral tangent linear parts and rational constants and is distinct. Definition 4.4 defines the PA measure as the full recursive zero-cycle, with no division by $d!$. Definition 3.23 specifies uniform PAPC regularization; our particular envelopes have the direct sequence $P+1/j$.

The checked source Proposition 6.13 asserts an envelope affine on the obstacle's one-dimensional structure. Its proof applies BBGS22 Proposition 5.13 to an open-cover locality argument. Neither that locality theorem nor a higher-dimensional or real-category extension is used here. The already known one-dimensional graph contact theorem and prior two-vertex review are comparison data only. In particular none of them grants graph-cylinder gluing or raw-competitor continuity. The finite support/decomposition theorem for already PA references from the earlier real-reference draft is also unused.

## Primitive-normal divisor algebra, supplied directly

For a rational cell $\sigma$, always use the saturated tangent lattice
$$N_\sigma=N\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\sigma-\sigma).$$
For a facet $\tau\prec\sigma$, choose an inward lift $n_{\sigma/\tau}\in N_\sigma$ of the primitive generator of $N_\sigma/N_\tau$. Balancing for a cycle $z$ means $\sum_{\sigma\succ\tau}z(\sigma)n_{\sigma/\tau}\in N_{\tau,\mathbb R}$. BMPS Definition 2.31 gives
$$
(a\cdot z)(\tau)=\sum_{\sigma\succ\tau}z(\sigma)a_{\sigma,\mathrm{lin}}(n_{\sigma/\tau})
-a_{\tau,\mathrm{lin}}\left(\sum_{\sigma\succ\tau}z(\sigma)n_{\sigma/\tau}\right). \tag{4}
$$
This formula makes sense for real affine coefficients and real weights. Changes of normal lift are tangential and cancel because the pieces agree on $\tau$. It is bilinear. Every ambient affine function has zero divisor on a balanced cycle. It depends only on incident germs, so is local on ordinary opens.

Here are proofs of the refinement, balancing and commutativity properties in BMPS Remark 2.33 and Lemmas 2.34--2.35, including their real scope. For refinement, at a new tested $(k-1)$-face whose minimal old face has dimension $k$, the two old-cell subdivisions have the same weight and linear part and opposite primitive quotient normals; their contributions cancel. If the minimal old face has dimension $k-1$, its saturated tangents and all inherited incident normal classes and contributions agree with the old formula. If it has dimension greater than $k$, the inherited $k$-weights vanish. These cases exhaust the possibilities. The same opposite-normal argument proves that an inherited balanced cycle is balanced on a refinement.

For the other two properties, take a $(k-2)$-face, quotient its saturated tangent lattice, subtract ambient linear extensions of the common tangential parts of the functions, and refine to pointed two-cones. Such a rational refinement exists by rational hyperplane cuts followed by a triangulation of a rational bounded section; cones with lineality can first be cut by rational coordinate hyperplanes. The quotient tangent lattices remain saturated: if a multiple of a quotient class is in the tangent subspace, saturation of the original larger tangent lattice puts the class there too.

Write the primitive boundary rays of a quotient two-cone as $u_r,u_s$, its weight as $\omega_{rs}$, and
$$\chi_{rs}=[N_{C_{rs}}:\mathbb Zu_r+\mathbb Zu_s].$$
Extend $u_r$ to a basis $(u_r,v)$ of the saturated plane lattice. Then $u_s=b u_r+\chi_{rs}v$ with the inward orientation. Thus the primitive normal is $u_s/\chi_{rs}$ modulo the tangent $\mathbb Ru_r$; this includes the actual index rather than replacing it by one. Balancing at $r$ reads
$$\sum_{C_{rs}\succ r}\frac{\omega_{rs}}{\chi_{rs}}u_s=t_ru_r.$$
Tangential cancellation in (4) gives
$$D_a(r)=\sum_{C_{rs}\succ r}\frac{\omega_{rs}}{\chi_{rs}}a(u_s)-t_ra(u_r).$$
Then $\sum_rD_a(r)u_r=0$: substituting the displayed balancing equation into the second sum cancels the first sum pair by pair in the unordered two-cones. The next divisor at the quotient origin is
$$
\sum_{\{r,s\}}\frac{\omega_{rs}}{\chi_{rs}}
\bigl(a(u_s)b(u_r)+a(u_r)b(u_s)\bigr)
-\sum_rt_ra(u_r)b(u_r). \tag{5}
$$
It is symmetric in $a,b$. This proves balancing and commutativity in every germ and hence globally, directly for real weights and coefficients. In particular the symmetric last term is retained. Refinement independence legitimizes all cuts made here and all later fan calculations.

For direct lattice factors, a product facet loses one dimension in exactly one factor. Its saturated tangent lattices split and its primitive normal is $(n,0)$ or $(0,n)$. Formula (4) therefore gives
$$ (a\circ p_Z)\cdot(Z\times Y)=(a\cdot Z)\times Y. \tag{6} $$
For the function $\sum_{i=1}^d|s_i|$ on a lattice-coordinate affine $d$-space of constant weight $c$, (6) and commutativity give mass $2^d d!c$ at the origin: each coordinate must occur once in the expansion. This states the normalization used throughout; no factorial or lattice index is removed. The proof below uses the whole recursive cycle and does not substitute a top-face-interior measure for it.

## Elementary finite-dimensional convex inputs

We supply the elementary facts needed in the envelope construction. A rational polyhedral cone has finitely many rational generators, including both signs of a basis of its rational lineality. Indeed, quotient the lineality. For a pointed cone given by $\ell_i\geq0$, $\ell=\sum_i\ell_i$ is positive away from zero, and the section $\ell=1$ is bounded: an unbounded sequence normalized on the sphere would limit to a nonzero vector with $\ell=0$, a contradiction. A bounded polyhedron is the convex hull of its vertices. To see this, a point in a positive-dimensional minimal face lies between terminal points in smaller faces; induction on face dimension reduces to vertices. There are finitely many vertices, obtained by full-rank active equations, and they are rational for rational data. Lift these generators and the lineality basis back. Homogenizing a nonempty pointed rational polyhedron as $\{(y,t):Ay\geq bt,t\geq0\}$ now gives
$$\sigma=\operatorname{conv}(A_\sigma)+\operatorname{cone}(R_\sigma), \tag{7}$$
with finite rational sets and nonempty $A_\sigma$.

Finite convex hulls plus finitely generated cones of real vectors are closed polyhedra. One proof eliminates variables from their finite nonstrict linear description: each variable is removed by comparing every lower bound with every upper bound, with one-sided bounds imposing no extra condition. This yields a finite nonstrict description of the projection, even with arbitrary real coefficients. Apply it to $x=\sum\alpha_ip_i+\sum t_jr_j$, $\alpha_i,t_j\geq0$, $\sum\alpha_i=1$. This also proves rationality of projections when all data are rational.

A finite rationally convex function on $\mathbb Q^n$ has a unique finite continuous convex completion to $\mathbb R^n$. On a rational box its corner values bound it above. If the centre is $c$, reflection and the midpoint inequality give $F(y)\geq2F(c)-F(2c-y)$, a uniform lower bound on a smaller box. In particular take bounds $L\leq F\leq M$ on $c+[-2R,2R]^n$ with rational $c,R$. For rational $y,z$ in $c+[-R/2,R/2]^n$, set $\delta=\|z-y\|_\infty$ and, when $\delta>0$, $T=R/\delta\geq1$. Both $T$ and $y+T(z-y)$ are rational and the latter stays in the larger box. Convexity gives $F(z)-F(y)\leq(M-L)\delta/R$; reverse the pair for the opposite bound. This proves local Lipschitz continuity and completion. Density proves convexity and uniqueness. The identical argument shows that a finite everywhere-defined convex function is continuous.

Such a function has an affine support at every point. For completeness, separate $(x,F(x)-\varepsilon)$ from the closed epigraph using the normal at its nearest epigraph point. Existence follows by minimizing distance on a sufficiently large compact ball, and the separating inequality follows by differentiating squared distance along segments. The normal's height coefficient is positive: it is nonnegative by the upward ray, and if zero its horizontal part would bound all of $\mathbb R^n$, which is impossible for a nonzero normal. Normalization gives an affine minorant with value between $F(x)-\varepsilon$ and $F(x)$ at $x$. Its slopes are bounded by evaluation at $x\pm Re_i$. A convergent subsequence as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives a support at $x$. These facts are also valid for $n=0$.

## A saturated global tree lift

Work first with a connected component. A positive local relation in (1) lies in the interior of the nonnegative orthant. If the full kernel of the direction map had dimension greater than one, a small perturbation of that positive vector by another kernel vector would remain positive and contradict (1). Hence for valence $k_v$ the local direction span has dimension $k_v-1$, and its only relation is the weighted balancing relation. Valence one is impossible. At valence two the primitive directions are opposite and the weights are equal. Suppress finite bivalent vertices; their affine strips and actual primitive lattices agree on both sides. If the carrier is a complete line, insert one rational bivalent vertex and use the same construction. After suppression a branching vertex has no opposite pair of outgoing directions: such a pair would give an independent relation unless the valence were two.

At each remaining vertex take the **actual saturated lattice**
$$\Lambda_v=N_G\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{v_{v,e}:e\ni v\}.$$
For each bounded edge glue the two copies of its primitive rank-one lattice with the sign appropriate to the opposite outgoing directions. The quotient of $\bigoplus_v\Lambda_v$ by these identifications is a free lattice $\widetilde N_G$. To prove this and saturation, root the tree and attach vertices one at a time. The incoming primitive vector at a child is part of a lattice basis, so write $\Lambda_{\rm child}=\mathbb Z v_{\rm in}\oplus C$. The new glued lattice is exactly the old lattice $\oplus C$. The parent edge vector is primitive in the old lattice because its parent vertex lattice is saturated there. The child lattice is then saturated, every earlier vertex lattice remains saturated, and its intersection with the preceding space is precisely the common rank-one edge lattice. This is an induction, with no ray-generated-lattice saturation assumption.

Choose a rational root position zero and integrate each lifted primitive direction along the original rational bounded-edge length. The tree has a unique path, so positions are well defined. This defines $\iota:G\to\widetilde G\subset\widetilde N_{G,\mathbb R}$. The homomorphism sending every $\Lambda_v$ back into $N_G$, and translating the root back, maps $\widetilde G$ to $G$ with the original edge parameters. It proves injectivity on the carrier. Near each vertex $\iota$ is an affine lattice isomorphism of the actual saturated local span onto a saturated sublattice of $\widetilde N_G$; on an edge it is the analogous primitive rank-one isomorphism. The product map leaves $E$ unchanged. A rational translation identifies $E$ with $N_{E,\mathbb R}$ without altering any condition.

Every convex polyhedron in a branching graph cylinder lies in one closed edge strip or a vertex fibre. Its graph projection is convex and contained in $G$; a segment cannot traverse a branching vertex because no two outgoing directions are opposite. The suppressed bivalent portions are single affine strips. Thus arbitrary rational spatial structures transfer in both directions under $\iota$. If a PCC centre lies over a vertex, all incident endpoint cells lie in the locally incident strips and the **one** local affine map preserves the barycentre. If its centre lies in an edge strip and its minimal graph face is nontrivial, all endpoints use that strip's affine map; the same holds for an edge-interior fibre centre. These statements apply to every rational structure, real centre and real coefficient, not only a chosen obstacle refinement. They preserve rational endpoints and face incidences in both directions, hence all raw PC classes. Locally they also identify every saturated cell tangent lattice and primitive quotient normal. Formula (4), weights, local cycles and every successive divisor are therefore preserved. This is a germwise lattice identification, not a nonproper pushforward assertion.

Let $V$ be the number of vertices, $B=V-1$ the number of bounded edges and $L$ the number of unbounded leaves. The lift has rank
$$\sum_v(k_v-1)-B=(2B+L-V)-B=L-1. \tag{8}$$
The leaf directions span it: summing weighted local balancing on one side of a cut edge expresses its weighted direction as a signed sum of that side's weighted leaf directions, and all local lattices are spanned over $\mathbb R$ by their directions. Summing balancing at all vertices gives
$$\sum_{\ell}w_\ell v_\ell=0. \tag{9}$$
By (8) this is the unique leaf relation. It is strictly positive. In particular the $L$ leaf vectors are affinely independent and their simplex contains zero strictly in its interior. Rational far leaf endpoints have form $b_\ell+T v_\ell$. Their simplices exhaust the ambient space as rational positive integers $T$ grow: divided by $T$, the vertices converge to the preceding simplex, which contains a ball about zero. Their product with rational affine boxes fills $\widetilde N_{G,\mathbb R}\oplus E$. Every ambient point is consequently in the convex hull of finitely many rational carrier points.

## Global scalar supports on the lifted tree

**Lemma 1.** Let $k$ be finite on the rational points of $\widetilde G$ and satisfy graph PCC inequalities at rational centres with **rational** coefficients. It has a continuous convex completion on each edge, agreeing with its vertex values, finite outgoing derivatives $m_{v,e}$, and
$$\sum_{e\ni v}w_em_{v,e}\geq0. \tag{10}$$
It has a global ambient affine minorant touching at every rational graph point.

**Proof.** Rational Jensen completes each interval in its interior. At an endpoint its one-sided limit is finite and at most the specified endpoint value: a secant from that endpoint gives the upper bound, and a supporting secant from an interior point gives a finite lower bound. For sufficiently small positive rational $t$, endpoints $v+t v_{v,e}$ give a vertex PCC with coefficients $w_e/\sum w_e$. Their limits are all at most $k(v)$, and the PCC inequality forces all of them to equal $k(v)$. Each outgoing derivative is bounded above by a finite secant. The same vertex inequality divided by $t$ rules out $-\infty$ for any derivative and gives (10).

To obtain a support touching a rational point $q$, insert $q$ as a bivalent vertex if necessary; this subdivision does not change the amalgamated lattice. At the root $q$, choose numbers $s_e\leq m_{q,e}$ with $\sum w_es_e=0$, possible by (10). At a bivalent root these are an ordinary pair of opposite supporting slopes. Give the affine function value $k(q)$ there.

Proceed away from the root. Suppose a parent edge's chosen slope in the direction toward a child $v$ is $s$. Convexity along that edge gives $s\leq k'_e(v-)$ and its continued support value at $v$ is at most $k(v)$. At $v$, (10) implies
$$\sum_{e\ {
m child}}w_em_{v,e}\geq w_{\rm parent}k'_e(v-)\geq w_{\rm parent}s.$$
Choose child slopes $s_e\leq m_{v,e}$ with weighted sum $w_{\rm parent}s$. There is always such a choice: take all upper bounds and subtract the nonnegative excess from one child slope. There is at least one child edge, possibly an unbounded ray, since no finite terminal vertex exists. Each child restriction stays below $k$, using its starting value at most $k(v)$ and slope at most its outgoing derivative. Finish at the finitely many vertices. Unbounded leaf convexity gives the inequality for the whole leaf, including remote points.

At each vertex the chosen slope vector annihilates its sole relation, so defines a linear form on the full local span. Forms on adjacent spans agree on the shared edge vector. By the lattice amalgamation they define one ambient real linear form, and the root intercept produces one global affine function. It lies below $k$ everywhere and touches at $q$. In particular a leaf-touching support has its actual possibly smaller intercept at its base vertex; no equality with that vertex's $k$-value is presumed. $\square$

## Every raw cylinder competitor has a global convex majorant

**Lemma 2.** For every finite raw PC $h$ on $\widetilde X=\widetilde G\times E$, there is a finite continuous ambient convex $H_h$ equal to $h$ at every rational carrier point, majorizing $h$ on all carrier points, and respecting every continuous upper bound on $h$. For continuous $h$ it is an exact extension on the carrier.

**Proof.** For rational graph $q$, complete the finite rationally convex slice $z\mapsto h(q,z)$ on $N_{E,\mathbb Q}$ to $F_q$ by the elementary convex fact. For a real dual vector $p$, set
$$ k_p(q)=\inf_{z\in N_{E,\mathbb Q}}(h(q,z)-p(z))\in[-\infty,\infty). \tag{11} $$
This obeys graph PCC inequalities with rational centres, rational endpoints and rational coefficients: choose rational $z_i$ approaching the infima, apply the actual cylinder PCC at the rational barycentre $(q,\sum a_iz_i)$, subtract $p$, and take infima. If one endpoint has infimum $-\infty$, vary only that endpoint while keeping the others finite. The rational-coefficient restriction here ensures that the affine barycentre remains rational; it does not restrict the actual PC tests used elsewhere.

If $k_p$ is finite at one rational point it is finite at every rational graph point. For an edge-interior finite centre, any other rational point on its edge is an endpoint of a rational same-edge convex combination, the other endpoint chosen on the other side. Thus no endpoint can have value $-\infty$. At a finite vertex, any chosen remote rational point $v+t_e v_{v,e}$ on an incident edge occurs in a vertex PCC with rational positive endpoints on all other incident edges: choose arbitrary rational positive $t_j$ within any bounded edge and coefficients proportional to $w_j/t_j$. These cancel directions. It cannot have value $-\infty$. Propagate across the connected finite graph. This proves the assertion including vertices, arbitrarily remote endpoints and unbounded rays.

At a rational $(q,z)$, choose a subgradient $p$ of $F_q$ at $z$. Then $k_p(q)=h(q,z)-p(z)$ is finite. Lemma 1 provides a global affine support $l$ of $k_p$ touching at $q$. Therefore $l(y)+p(z')$ lies below $h$ at every rational carrier point and touches at $(q,z)$. Take the supremum of all these touching affine minorants. It is finite everywhere: far-leaf simplices times rational affine boxes bound every minorant above at any prescribed ambient point by a convex average of finitely many finite $h$-values. One minorant gives a finite lower bound. Thus $H_h$ is finite convex and continuous, and equals $h$ on rational carrier points.

For a real point $x$ choose its minimal face in a rational structure. If zero-dimensional it is rational. Otherwise small simplices with rational vertices in that face contain $x$ and shrink to it; construct them by rational approximation of a small enclosing simplex in the rational affine hull. Their real barycentric coefficients are actual same-cell PCCs. The raw inequality and continuity of $H_h$ give $h(x)\leq H_h(x)$. Every continuous upper bound on $h$ holds for $H_h$ on the carrier by equality at rational points and density. If $h$ is continuous these two directions give exact equality. $\square$

## Actual envelopes and finite rational spatial domains

Transport $\gamma,u$ to the lift; write $f=\gamma+u$ and choose $C\geq\|u\|_\infty$. Lemma 2 gives an exact finite ambient convex extension $g$ of $\gamma$. On a common finite rational reference/obstacle structure, every cell is pointed: a nonzero lineality vector would give two opposite recession vectors and reference slopes, contradicting positivity. For each spatial cell use (7). Its obstacle epigraph is generated by point vectors $(y,f(y))$, ray vectors $(r,f_{\sigma,\mathrm{lin}}(r))$ and the upward vertical ray. Their finite unions $\mathcal A,\mathcal R$ have rational **spatial** coordinates, but arbitrary real heights. Then
$$
K=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\{(x,t):x\in\widetilde X,\ t\geq f(x)\}
=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)+\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal R). \tag{12}
$$
The right side is closed by elimination and contains all epigraph pieces. Conversely any recession generator can be added to a convex-hull point by a limit: use weight $\varepsilon$ on a far point of its epigraph piece with distance scaled by $1/\varepsilon$, and weight $1-\varepsilon$ on the given point. Repeat for finitely many generators. This proves both inclusions in (12).

Its spatial projection is the whole lifted ambient space by far-leaf filling. It lies in $\operatorname{epi}(g-C)$, so every fibre is a closed upward ray with a finite lower endpoint. Thus $K=\operatorname{epi}(H)$ for a finite convex polyhedral $H$. Elimination expresses its epigraph by finitely many inequalities. Since it is upward and has full spatial projection, the nontrivial inequalities all have positive height coefficient, so $H$ is the maximum of finitely many affine planes. The function is the greatest ambient convex minorant of $f$ on the carrier, because the epigraph of any such minorant is closed convex and contains every obstacle epigraph point. Hence
$$\gamma-C\leq H|_{\widetilde X}\leq f\leq\gamma+C. \tag{13}$$
Every raw competitor $h$ has the majorant $H_h$ of Lemma 2, respecting $f$ and $\gamma+C_h$. The greatest-minorant property gives $h\leq H_h|_{\widetilde X}\leq H|_{\widetilde X}$. Conversely the restriction of $H$ satisfies every actual PCC by ordinary ambient Jensen, lies below $f$ and has the required growth by (13). This proves the exact raw envelope equality
$$P_\gamma(u)=H|_{\widetilde X}. \tag{14}$$
There is no continuity or locality assumption about raw competitors in this argument.

Rational spatial domains require a separate proof. Every lower graph face of $K$ is the convex hull of the subset of $\mathcal A$ on its supporting graph plane plus the cone of the subset of $\mathcal R$ on that plane. All generator slacks are nonnegative, and positive coefficients on a face force zero slack. Its spatial projection therefore has a finite rational point/ray representation. Projection is an affine isomorphism on a graph face and preserves intersections and faces, because the lower graph height is unique. The projections of all lower graph faces are a finite rational complex covering ambient space, on each of whose cells $H$ is real affine. Intersect with carrier strips and transfer back. This proves the promised finite rational structure for $P$. Arbitrary real maxima have not been declared rational-domain PA.

Finally $P$ is PAPC against every nonnegative local real cycle of every positive dimension. At a tested face pick a relative-interior point and an ambient supporting plane for $H$. Subtract that plane. The residual tangential linear part vanishes and every inward derivative of each incident piece is nonnegative, by convexity. Formula (4) is a nonnegative weighted sum. The local lattice maps carry this test back to the original carrier and every ordinary open. Consequently successive divisors remain nonnegative balanced cycles. Their $d$-fold zero-cycle is finite atomic on the finite rational domain vertices. The uniform decreasing sequence $P+1/j$ is in the same PAPC growth class and has identical divisors, establishing the actual real regularizable domain for this envelope.

## Two full recursive vanishing mechanisms

We will use the following elementary consequences of (4) on complete local rational function-domain fans. They concern the entire local cycle.

**Quotient vanishing.** Suppose that after subtracting an ambient affine function, a germ on a local $d$-cycle is the pullback of a function defined on an entire rational quotient space of dimension $q<d$, affine on a finite complete rational fan there. Let $T_j$ be the union of quotient fan faces of codimension at least $j$. The first divisor has support in the inverse image of $T_1$, because off its walls the function is affine and balancing makes (4) zero. Inductively, at the relative interior of a codimension-$(j-1)$ face, the previous cycle is locally supported in that face's inverse image, where the function is affine, so its next divisor is zero. Thus the $j$th divisor has support in the inverse image of $T_j$. As $T_{q+1}$ is empty and $q+1\leq d$, the top divisor vanishes. Common rational refinements justify these computations.

**Lineality vanishing.** If the carrier fan and the function-domain fan have a common nonzero rational lineality space, retain it in a common generalized fan. Every face contains that space and there are no zero-dimensional faces. All successive divisors live on that fan, so their top zero-cycle is zero. Refinement cannot create an atom. An ambient affine term may first be removed.

## Branch sums replace the two-vertex case analysis

We now prove the global tree fact that makes contact work at every junction. Fix a rational graph point $q$, insert it as a bivalent vertex if needed, and root the amalgamation there. Write $S_q$ for its local graph direction span, of dimension $r=k_q-1$. Rooted lattice attachment gives a real direct decomposition
$$\widetilde N_{G,\mathbb R}=S_q\oplus\bigoplus_{e\ni q}V_e. \tag{15}$$
Here $V_e$ is the direct sum of the complements attached at all descendants in branch $e$. Any graph displacement $y-q$ in that branch, and any leaf recession direction of that branch, belongs to $\mathbb Rv_{q,e}\oplus V_e$: integrate its unique path, starting with $v_{q,e}$, and use the successive attached complements. Root reinsertion changes neither the amalgamated lattice nor this assertion.

Suppose a positive combination of selected graph displacements and selected nonnegative leaf recession directions sums to zero. Group the selected terms by the components of $G\setminus\{q\}$, and call the group sums $B_e$. Terms with zero graph displacement do not matter. By the direct decomposition (15), every $B_e$ is of the form $b_ev_{q,e}$: its $V_e$ component must vanish, since no other branch can cancel it.

Moreover $b_e\geq0$, with strict positivity if that branch contains any nonzero selected graph term. To prove the sign, construct a linear form on $\mathbb Rv_{q,e}\oplus V_e$ with value one on $v_{q,e}$ and positive value on every direction oriented away from $q$ in this branch. At a descendant, if its incoming edge has outward-parent slope $s>0$, give every child edge the positive slope
$$s_{\rm child}=w_{\rm parent}s/\sum_{\rm child}w_{\rm child}.$$
The local weighted relation is annihilated, and the forms agree on shared edges, so define a linear form on the amalgamation. Every point displacement in the branch has positive value, being a path with positive lengths and positive slopes, and every leaf direction has positive value. Evaluation on $B_e=b_ev_{q,e}$ proves the assertion. This is a finite construction; it does not assert a globally positive harmonic function on the whole graph.

The unique local relation then gives
$$ (b_e)_e=c(w_e)_e,\qquad c\geq0. \tag{16}$$
If any graph term is nonzero, $c>0$ and all branches contribute. This branch-sum statement also works at bounded-edge interiors, unbounded-edge interiors and artificially inserted bivalent vertices. It uses the full amalgamated tree space, so includes arbitrarily remote selected generators.

## Every noncontact atom has zero full coefficient

Let $x=(q,z)$ be any possible atom in the finite rational structure for $P$, and suppose $H(x)<f(x)$. Its coordinates are rational. Choose a generator representation, omitting zero coefficients,
$$
(x,H(x))=\sum_j\alpha_j(y_j,f(y_j))+\sum_\nu t_\nu(r_\nu,s_\nu),
\quad \alpha_j>0,\quad\sum_j\alpha_j=1,\quad t_\nu>0. \tag{17}
$$
Every active lower plane at $x$ has nonnegative slack on the generators, and the total slack is zero. Thus every selected generator lies on every active plane. The upward vertical ray has positive slack and cannot be selected. Define the rational spatial space
$$\mathcal L=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{y_j-x,r_\nu\}. \tag{18}$$
It is nonzero: if all spatial generators vanished, every selected point would be $x$ and (17) would force $H(x)=f(x)$. All differences of active slopes annihilate $\mathcal L$. Inactive planes stay strictly below in a small neighbourhood. After subtraction of an active affine plane, the germ is therefore invariant under $\mathcal L$.

The active-domain fan is rational. Indeed the global domains already have rational spatial faces; their tangent cones at rational $x$ give a rational refinement of the coarsest active fan. Each coarsest cone is a convex union of those finitely many rational cones, hence is generated by finitely many rational vectors. Its lineality contains $\mathcal L$. Intersecting with a rational subspace and quotienting by a rational part of $\mathcal L$ supplies complete rational quotient fans.

Put $W_q=S_q\oplus E$, the ambient local tangent space of the carrier at $x$. The graph projection of (17) says
$$\sum_j\alpha_j(y_{j,G}-q)+\sum_\nu t_\nu r_{\nu,G}=0. \tag{19}$$
Every nonzero graph recession term is a nonnegative multiple of a leaf direction: a spatial cell is in an edge strip, so a bounded edge has zero graph recession and an unbounded edge has only its outgoing ray. Group the full vectors $\alpha_j(y_j-x)$ and $t_\nu r_\nu$ according to these graph branches. Each group sum $U_e$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. By (15) and (19) its graph projection is $b_ev_{q,e}$, so actually
$$U_e\in\mathcal L\cap W_q.$$ 
If there is any nonzero selected graph term, the branch-sum proof gives $b_e=cw_e>0$ for all incident edges. The projections of these $U_e$ span all of $S_q$. Consequently
$$\dim(\mathcal L\cap W_q)\geq r,\qquad
\dim\bigl(W_q/(\mathcal L\cap W_q)\bigr)\leq m<d. \tag{20}$$
The residual germ on the entire $W_q$ is the maximum of active linear forms annihilating $\mathcal L\cap W_q$, and hence is defined on that whole quotient with its finite complete rational domain fan. Quotient vanishing applies to the **full** local graph-cylinder $d$-cycle, including all its lower-face terms.

If there is no nonzero selected graph term, all selected point graph coordinates equal $q$ and every selected ray has zero graph coordinate. Then $0\ne\mathcal L\subset E$. The local graph-cylinder carrier has $E$ as lineality and the residual function fan has $\mathcal L$ as lineality, so lineality vanishing applies. The case $m=0$ cannot have this second alternative at noncontact.

These two alternatives exhaust every possible noncontact atom: branching vertices of arbitrary valence, original or inserted bivalent vertices, edge junctions, interiors of bounded edges and all unbounded leaves, with all affine-coordinate domain faces. Local lattice identifications preserve their complete recursive coefficients on the original carrier. Its positive finite atomic measure therefore has no support outside contact. The integrand in (2) is bounded by (13) and vanishes at every remaining atom. The complete integral is exactly zero. For finitely many connected tree components the arguments apply componentwise: a PCC's incident cell belongs to one component, local cycles do likewise, and their finitely many measures add. This proves the theorem.

## Why cycles and the original classification remain open

The tree assumption enters twice in essential global assertions: the lattice attachment adds independent branch complements with no closure constraints, and the scalar support construction visits each vertex once without a conflicting return condition. The proof supplies neither assertion for a graph cycle. A cyclic graph cannot simply be cut and glued: its closed spatial walk imposes a rational length-weighted direction relation in addition to the local balancing relations, and its harmonic affine supports must have zero period. Losing the independent branch decomposition can invalidate (16)--(20).

An explicit diagnostic is the unit-weight triangular graph with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)$, three bounded edges of primitive length one, and outgoing leaves $(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)$ at these vertices respectively. Each star is rank-one trivalent and every local lattice is saturated. If $a,b,c$ denote oriented cycle directions $A\to B$, $B\to C$, $C\to A$, the formal amalgamation using only edge identifications and local relations has independent $a,b,c$, with leaf vectors $c-a$, $a-b$, $b-c$. Integrating around the bounded cycle ends at $a+b+c$, which is nonzero there. An actual lift of the closed carrier requires the extra relation $a+b+c=0$. Its rank drops from three to two, and the independent tree branches are no longer available. This proves failure of that particular proposed construction, **not** a failure of regularizability or contact on the triangular cylinder.

The partial-Legendre finite graph LP remains an unproved alternative for cycles. Interior obstacle breakpoints, unbounded rays, joint graph/affine convexity, exact raw competitors, rational spatial walls and full vertex contact all require proof. A failed LP or lift is not an actual contact counterexample. No cyclic envelope/contact theorem is claimed here.

The controlling book already proves the finite one-dimensional graph criterion, including cycles. The previously reviewed two-vertex theorem already treats one specified unit-weight tree times all complete affine dimensions. The present contribution is the arbitrary-tree extension with general rational weights, lengths, valences and actual local lattice indices, every permitted real reference and every bounded real-PA obstacle. Its new global ingredients are saturated tree amalgamation, recursive scalar supports and the branch-sum annihilation argument. It neither repeats the one-dimensional criterion as new nor claims arbitrary balanced-pair classification. Original P05.2 remains open; status is **partial**, candidate is **false**. No conclusion for the literal coefficient category follows, even when the input functions happen to be literal.
